## Description

Primary source:

<https://ngs101.com/how-to-analyze-single-cell-rna-seq-data-complete-beginners-guide-part-4-cell-type-identification/>

Part 3 of 3. The four annotations from parts 1-2 (manual, SingleR, scType,
scCATCH) are compared by confusion matrix, alluvial (Sankey-style) plot and
side-by-side UMAP. A cluster-level table is exported for manual review; a
consensus label is added by hand and imported to produce the final annotation.

Rule of thumb used in the article for the manual review: 4/4 methods agree ->
accept; 3/4 -> usually accept after checking markers; 2/4 -> investigate;
no agreement -> manual review.

Code is taken from the source article's code blocks (steps 15-20). Changes made
for this notebook series: hard-coded values moved into the YAML front matter,
paths built from `params` rather than `setwd()`, and changes marked `ADDED:` or
`FIX:` in comments.

## Libraries and directories

```{r step1_libs_data}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: Load required libraries
#-----------------------------------------------

# Core single-cell analysis
library(Seurat)
library(SeuratObject)

# Visualization and data manipulation
library(ggplot2)
library(ggalluvial)
library(dplyr)
library(patchwork)
library(scales)
library(viridis)

if (!exists("params") || !is.list(params)) {
  # Running interactively (e.g. via "Run Cell") rather than through
  # knit/render, so `params` was never created by rmarkdown::render().
  # Reconstruct it by parsing this .Rmd's own YAML header, so the params
  # defaults live in exactly one place (the YAML block above) instead of
  # being duplicated here.
  rmd_path <- tryCatch(
    # Only reliable when this document is the active editor tab; if focus
    # has moved to another file, this will pick up the wrong path.
    rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()$path,
    error = function(e) NA_character_
  )
  if (is.na(rmd_path) || !nzchar(rmd_path)) {
    # Fallback if rstudioapi is unavailable or no doc is focused; assumes
    # the working directory is the project root.
    rmd_path <- "scRNAseq_tutorial_4_cell_type_annotation/tut4_cell_type_annotation_part3.Rmd"
  }
  params <- rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter(rmd_path)$params
}

# Set working directory

# Create output directories

  if (!dir.exists(file.path(annot.dir, d))) dir.create(file.path(annot.dir, d), recursive = TRUE)
}

# Set random seed for reproducibility

# Configure plotting defaults
theme_set(theme_classic(base_size = 12))

cluster.col <- params$cluster.col
sample.col <- params$sample.col

patient.col <- params$patient.col
```

## Confusion matrices

Cell-level cross-tabulation of each automated method against the manual
annotation.

```{r step3_confusion}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 15: Generate confusion matrices
#-----------------------------------------------

# Function to create confusion matrix
# FIX: the article's version of this function is cut off on the page (no
# return value and no closing brace, so the calls below would be swallowed
# into the function body); completed here
create_confusion_matrix <- function(method1_labels, method2_labels,
                                   method1_name, method2_name) {
  conf_table <- table(
    Method1 = method1_labels,
    Method2 = method2_labels
  )

  cat("\n===", method1_name, "(rows) vs.", method2_name, "(columns) ===\n")
  print(conf_table)

  return(conf_table)
}

# Compare each automated method to manual
conf_manual_vs_singler <- create_confusion_matrix(
  integrated_seurat$manual_annotation,
  integrated_seurat$singler_annotation,
  "Manual", "SingleR"
)

conf_manual_vs_sctype <- create_confusion_matrix(
  integrated_seurat$manual_annotation,
  integrated_seurat$sctype_annotation,
  "Manual", "scType"
)

conf_manual_vs_sccatch <- create_confusion_matrix(
  integrated_seurat$manual_annotation,
  integrated_seurat$sccatch_annotation,
  "Manual", "scCATCH"
)

# Save confusion matrices
write.csv(conf_manual_vs_singler,
          file.path(annot.dir, "annotations/confusion_matrix_manual_vs_singler.csv"))
write.csv(conf_manual_vs_sctype,
          file.path(annot.dir, "annotations/confusion_matrix_manual_vs_sctype.csv"))
write.csv(conf_manual_vs_sccatch,
          file.path(annot.dir, "annotations/confusion_matrix_manual_vs_sccatch.csv"))
```

## Sankey diagrams

```{r step4_sankey, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 10}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 16: Create Sankey diagrams
#-----------------------------------------------

# Function to prepare Sankey data
prepare_sankey_data <- function(method1_labels, method2_labels,
                               method1_name, method2_name) {
  sankey_df <- data.frame(
    Method1 = method1_labels,
    Method2 = method2_labels
  ) %>%
    group_by(Method1, Method2) %>%
    summarise(Count = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(Comparison = paste(method1_name, "vs", method2_name))

  return(sankey_df)
}

# Prepare data for each comparison
sankey_manual_singler <- prepare_sankey_data(
  integrated_seurat$manual_annotation,
  integrated_seurat$singler_annotation,
  "Manual", "SingleR"
)

sankey_manual_sctype <- prepare_sankey_data(
  integrated_seurat$manual_annotation,
  integrated_seurat$sctype_annotation,
  "Manual", "scType"
)

sankey_manual_sccatch <- prepare_sankey_data(
  integrated_seurat$manual_annotation,
  integrated_seurat$sccatch_annotation,
  "Manual", "scCATCH"
)

# Function to create Sankey plot
create_sankey_plot <- function(sankey_data, method1_name, method2_name) {
  p <- ggplot(sankey_data,
              aes(axis1 = Method1, axis2 = Method2, y = Count)) +
    geom_alluvium(aes(fill = Method1), width = params$sankey.width, alpha = params$sankey.alpha) +
    geom_stratum(width = params$sankey.width, fill = "white", color = "grey") +
    geom_text(stat = "stratum", aes(label = after_stat(stratum)),
              size = 3, fontface = "bold") +
    scale_x_discrete(limits = c(method1_name, method2_name),
                     expand = c(0.05, 0.05)) +
    labs(title = paste(method1_name, "vs", method2_name),
         subtitle = "Straight flows = agreement | Crossed flows = disagreement",
         y = "Number of Cells") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "none",
          axis.text.y = element_blank(),
          axis.title.x = element_blank(),
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

  return(p)
}

# Create Sankey plots
p_sankey_singler <- create_sankey_plot(sankey_manual_singler, "Manual", "SingleR")
print(p_sankey_singler)
ggsave(file.path(annot.dir, "plots/method_comparison/14_sankey_manual_vs_singler.png"),
       p_sankey_singler, width = 12, height = 10, dpi = params$plot.dpi)

p_sankey_sctype <- create_sankey_plot(sankey_manual_sctype, "Manual", "scType")
print(p_sankey_sctype)
ggsave(file.path(annot.dir, "plots/method_comparison/15_sankey_manual_vs_sctype.png"),
       p_sankey_sctype, width = 12, height = 10, dpi = params$plot.dpi)

p_sankey_sccatch <- create_sankey_plot(sankey_manual_sccatch, "Manual", "scCATCH")
print(p_sankey_sccatch)
ggsave(file.path(annot.dir, "plots/method_comparison/16_sankey_manual_vs_sccatch.png"),
       p_sankey_sccatch, width = 12, height = 10, dpi = params$plot.dpi)
```

## Side-by-side UMAP comparison

```{r step5_umap_compare, fig.width = 18, fig.height = 14}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 17: Create comprehensive UMAP comparison
#-----------------------------------------------

# Create individual plots with consistent styling
p_manual_comp <- DimPlot(
  integrated_seurat,
  reduction = umap_reduction,
  group.by = "manual_annotation",
  pt.size = 0.1
) +
  labs(title = "Manual") +
  theme(legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

p_singler_comp <- DimPlot(
  integrated_seurat,
  reduction = umap_reduction,
  group.by = "singler_annotation",
  pt.size = 0.1
) +
  labs(title = "SingleR (Monaco)") +
  theme(legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

p_sctype_comp <- DimPlot(
  integrated_seurat,
  reduction = umap_reduction,
  group.by = "sctype_annotation",
  pt.size = 0.1
) +
  labs(title = "scType (Markers)") +
  theme(legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

p_sccatch_comp <- DimPlot(
  integrated_seurat,
  reduction = umap_reduction,
  group.by = "sccatch_annotation",
  pt.size = 0.1
) +
  labs(title = "scCATCH (Tissue DB)") +
  theme(legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

# Combine all four methods
p_all_methods <- (p_manual_comp | p_singler_comp) /
                 (p_sctype_comp | p_sccatch_comp)
print(p_all_methods)

ggsave(file.path(annot.dir, "plots/method_comparison/17_all_methods_comparison.png"),
       p_all_methods, width = 18, height = 14, dpi = params$plot.dpi)
```

## Build consensus annotations

### Step 1: Export annotations for manual review

```{r step6_export}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 18: Export annotations for manual comparison
#-----------------------------------------------

# Create comprehensive annotation table
annotation_comparison <- data.frame(
  cell_barcode = colnames(integrated_seurat),
  cluster = integrated_seurat@meta.data[[cluster.col]],
  manual = integrated_seurat$manual_annotation,
  singler = integrated_seurat$singler_annotation,
  sctype = integrated_seurat$sctype_annotation,
  sccatch = integrated_seurat$sccatch_annotation,
  sample_id = integrated_seurat@meta.data[[sample.col]],
  condition = integrated_seurat@meta.data[[condition.col]],
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Export to CSV for manual review
write.csv(annotation_comparison,
          file.path(annot.dir, "annotations/all_methods_comparison.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

# Create cluster-level summary (easier to review)
cluster_summary <- annotation_comparison %>%
  group_by(cluster) %>%
  summarise(
    n_cells = n(),
    manual_type = names(sort(table(manual), decreasing = TRUE))[1],
    singler_type = names(sort(table(singler), decreasing = TRUE))[1],
    sctype_type = names(sort(table(sctype), decreasing = TRUE))[1],
    sccatch_type = names(sort(table(sccatch), decreasing = TRUE))[1],
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# FIX: do not overwrite a cluster-level file you have already edited (re-running
# this chunk after adding the consensus_annotation column would discard it)
cluster_comparison.file <- file.path(annot.dir, "annotations/cluster_level_comparison.csv")
already_edited <- file.exists(cluster_comparison.file) &&
  "consensus_annotation" %in% colnames(read.csv(cluster_comparison.file, nrows = 1))
if (already_edited) {
  message("Keeping existing ", cluster_comparison.file, " (has a consensus_annotation column)")
} else {
  write.csv(cluster_summary, cluster_comparison.file, row.names = FALSE)
}

print(as.data.frame(cluster_summary), row.names = FALSE)
```

### Step 2: Manual comparison

Open `annotations/cluster_level_comparison.csv` (in the tutorial 4 output
directory) in a spreadsheet, add a column named `consensus_annotation`, and fill
in a label for each cluster using method agreement together with the marker
evidence from part 1. Save it as CSV, then run the remaining chunks. They are
skipped while the column is missing or empty.

### Step 3: Import consensus and finalize

```{r step7_import, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 8}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 19: Import consensus annotations
#-----------------------------------------------

# Read your manually edited cluster consensus file
# (Save your Excel/Google Sheets file as CSV first)
cluster_consensus <- read.csv(cluster_comparison.file,
                              stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# ADDED: skip the rest if the consensus column has not been filled in yet
have_consensus <- "consensus_annotation" %in% colnames(cluster_consensus) &&
  any(!is.na(cluster_consensus$consensus_annotation) & nzchar(cluster_consensus$consensus_annotation))

if (have_consensus) {
  # Create mapping from cluster to consensus annotation
  cluster_to_consensus <- setNames(
    cluster_consensus$consensus_annotation,  # Column you created
    cluster_consensus$cluster
  )

  # Apply consensus to all cells
  integrated_seurat$final_annotation <- unname(cluster_to_consensus[
    as.character(integrated_seurat@meta.data[[cluster.col]])
  ])

  # Visualize final consensus
  p_consensus <- DimPlot(
    integrated_seurat,
    reduction = umap_reduction,
    group.by = "final_annotation",
    label = TRUE,
    label.size = 4,
    pt.size = 0.1,
    repel = TRUE
  ) +
    ggtitle("Final Consensus Annotation") +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))
  print(p_consensus)

  ggsave(file.path(annot.dir, "plots/method_comparison/18_final_consensus_annotation.png"),
         p_consensus, width = 11, height = 8, dpi = params$plot.dpi)
} else {
  message("No consensus_annotation values in ", cluster_comparison.file,
          "; fill it in and re-run from this chunk.")
}
```

```{r step7b_import_split, fig.width = 14, fig.height = 6, eval = have_consensus}
# Split by condition to check biological validity
p_consensus_split <- DimPlot(
  integrated_seurat,
  reduction = umap_reduction,
  group.by = "final_annotation",
  split.by = condition.col,
  pt.size = 0.1,
  ncol = 2
) +
  ggtitle("Final Consensus by Condition")
print(p_consensus_split)

ggsave(file.path(annot.dir, "plots/method_comparison/19_consensus_by_condition.png"),
       p_consensus_split, width = 14, height = 6, dpi = params$plot.dpi)
```

## Save annotated data

```{r step8_save, eval = have_consensus}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 20: Save final annotated Seurat object
#-----------------------------------------------

# Save the complete annotated Seurat object
saveRDS(integrated_seurat, file.path(annot.dir, "annotations/integrated_annotated_seurat.rds"))

# Create metadata export
metadata_export <- integrated_seurat@meta.data %>%
  select(
    all_of(c(sample.col, condition.col, patient.col)),
    all_of(cluster.col),
    manual_annotation,
    singler_annotation,
    sctype_annotation,
    sccatch_annotation,
    final_annotation
  )

write.csv(metadata_export,
          file.path(annot.dir, "annotations/cell_metadata_final.csv"),
          row.names = TRUE)
```
